did_you_know.text: At the beginning of the psalm, David presents the LORD through three images: “my light,” “my salvation,” and “the stronghold of my life.” He then asks twice, “Whom shall I fear?” and “Of whom shall I be afraid?”
The enemies are described figuratively as coming “to devour my flesh,” but those who oppose and attack him will ultimately stumble and fall.
David describes two dangerous situations—a camp encamped against him and a war waged against him—and declares that even in these circumstances his heart will not fear, because he trusts in God.
David defines his primary request with the word “one”: to dwell in the house of the LORD all the days of his life, to gaze upon the beauty of the LORD, and to visit His temple.

The verse depicts the LORD’s protection through several images: being hidden in a shelter, taking refuge in the secrecy of His tent, and being set high upon a rock. Together, they express security in the day of trouble.

After describing his deliverance, David describes his response: his head will be lifted above his enemies, and he will offer sacrifices with joyful shouts in the LORD’s tent and sing and make music to the LORD.
The verse presents a dialogue of spiritual seeking: the heart hears the call, “Seek my face,” and responds, “Your face, LORD, I will seek.”

Even in the difficult situation where his father and mother abandon him, David expresses faith that the LORD will take him in. This highlights the LORD’s faithfulness as a source of support and refuge.
David asks not to be handed over to his enemies and mentions two threats: false witnesses rising against him and those who breathe out violence against him.
The psalm ends with a double call: “Wait for the LORD.” Alongside hope, it mentions strength and courage, teaching perseverance in faith.
